title: Translation Software
overview: Translation software turns source code into executable behaviour. At A2 you need interpreters and compiler stages—lexical analysis, syntax analysis, code generation and optimisation—plus grammar description using BNF/syntax diagrams and expression evaluation using Reverse Polish Notation.
syllabusPoints: Explain interpreter operation and contrast it with compiled translation.
Describe lexical analysis, syntax analysis, code generation and optimisation.
Interpret or construct simple grammar using BNF/syntax diagrams.
Convert/evaluate expressions using Reverse Polish Notation and a stack.

definitions.definition: A classified unit produced during lexical analysis, e.g. keyword, identifier, literal or operator.
The actual character sequence that matches a token category.
The syntax-analysis component that checks tokens against grammar.
A formal notation that defines valid language structures using production rules.
Postfix notation where operators follow operands, allowing stack-based evaluation without brackets.
Transformation of generated/intermediate code to improve speed/size without changing its result.

sections.title: Interpreter
content: An interpreter translates/executes source during runtime and normally does not produce a permanently stored complete executable. It is convenient for testing and portable source execution, but repeated translation can reduce execution speed.

sections.title: Lexical analysis
content: The compiler scans source characters, groups them into tokens, discards irrelevant whitespace/comments where appropriate, recognises identifiers/literals and maintains symbol-table information. Invalid character sequences can be reported as lexical errors.

sections.title: Syntax analysis
content: The parser checks whether the token stream fits the language grammar, often building a parse tree/internal representation. Missing delimiters or malformed statements are syntax errors; logical correctness is a different issue.

sections.title: Code generation and optimisation
content: Once the source is valid, machine/intermediate instructions are generated. Optimisation can remove redundant work, improve instruction selection or reduce code size while preserving program behaviour.

sections.title: BNF and syntax diagrams
content: Both define legal grammatical structures. BNF uses production rules with sequences, alternatives and recursive definitions. Exam questions may ask whether a string is valid or to complete a rule.

sections.title: Reverse Polish Notation
content: Push operands onto a stack. When an operator appears, pop its operands, apply it, then push the result. No brackets are needed because order is explicit.

examTips: Remember the translation sequence: lexical -> syntax -> code generation -> optimisation.
For RPN subtraction/division, operand order matters: the first popped value is normally the right operand.
Syntax analysis checks grammar, not whether the algorithm gives the correct result.
commonMistakes: Confusing lexical errors with logic errors.
Saying an interpreter always creates a standalone executable.
